notes: Anthropic prices were taken at D2 from the claude-api skill model table (cached 2026-09-25): Opus 5.5 $4/$20 per MTok, cache read $0.20; Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, cache read $0.20. Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5, cache read $0.10) is not in that table. Cache writes use the 1.25x input rate (5-minute TTL). The official page (source URL) could not be fetched from the D2 environment: every entry with priceVerification 'pending-official-page' must be re-checked against the source before M2 sign-off. If a number differs, add a new catalog version file; never edit this one.

OpenAI entry added in D6 (2026-09-30) from the official pricing page https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (platform.openai.com/docs/pricing 301-redirects there) and the model page https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol, both fetched 2026-09-30. gpt-6.1-sol standard tier (prompts up to 272K input tokens): $2 input, $0.10 cached input, $2.50 cache write, $10 output per MTok; the changelog lists the release and these prices on 2026-09-29 (effectiveDate). Above 272K input tokens OpenAI charges 2x input/cache and 1.5x output, so maxInputTokens is deliberately capped at 272000 (the model's window is 1,050,000): capability validation blocks long-context prompts and the standard prices are provably the billed prices. Reasoning effort levels per the model page: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max ('none' is not listed, so reasoning is always on). supportsTokenCounting: POST /v1/responses/input_tokens (openai SDK 7.25 client.responses.inputTokens.count). Gemini entries are added in D10.

Gemini entry added in D10 (2026-09-30) from the official pricing page https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (page footer: Last updated 2026-10-01 UTC) and the model page https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.5-flash, both fetched 2026-09-30. gemini-3.5-flash Standard paid tier: $1.50 input, $9.00 output (including thinking tokens), $0.15 context caching per MTok; no prompt-length tiers (no price cliff, so maxInputTokens is the model's real 1,048,576 input limit; output limit 65,536). The changelog lists the GA release on 2026-05-19 (effectiveDate) with no later price change; the deprecations page lists no shutdown date. cacheWrite: Gemini has no per-token cache-write charge (implicit caching is free to write; explicit caches bill storage per hour, which Relay never creates, and the adapter always reports 0 cache-write tokens), so it is set to the input rate, which leaves upperBound unchanged. Thinking levels per https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking: minimal, low, medium (default), high; Relay maps low/medium/high (thinking cannot be turned off). Flex/Batch/Priority tiers bill differently: the adapter always sends serviceTier: 'standard' (@google/genai GenerateContentConfig.serviceTier, sent as the top-level request serviceTier) and flags priceTierMismatch when the reported usageMetadata.serviceTier is anything other than standard/unspecified (or, on Vertex, usageMetadata.trafficType is anything other than ON_DEMAND/TRAFFIC_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED). gemini-3.8-flash (newest stable Flash) was NOT chosen: its prices are introductory through 2026-12-31 and double on 2027-01-01, which one catalog entry cannot express honestly. supportsTokenCounting: models.countTokens (contents only on the Developer API).

2026-10-01: capabilities.priceCliffInputTokens added (not a price change; every price is unchanged). It records the prompt-length price tier the notes above already document: 272000 for gpt-6.1-sol (OpenAI standard tier up to 272K input tokens). No other entry documents a prompt-length tier in these notes (gemini-3.5-flash explicitly has none). Adapters use it to choose the conservative local input bound when a token count fails (plans/04 D1, ADR note 'Count-failure fallback').
